note.question: When can a merger of on-demand platforms improve consumer surplus and independent-worker welfare despite reducing price and wage competition?
note.overview: Before the merger, two on-demand platforms simultaneously compete in customer prices and agent wages while anticipating two-sided participation. The paper characterizes the Nash equilibrium and compares it with the merged firm's joint optimum.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: In the premerger game, the two platforms simultaneously choose customer prices and agent wages. Customers and agents then choose a platform or the outside option, generating a two-sided participation fixed point. In the postmerger counterfactual, one firm jointly chooses a common price and wage for the two retained platforms and pools agents to serve demand from both. Premerger platforms compete on both customer and worker sides.
